proposals.before: From the time writing was first made, what we can still know of the ancients through the Classics and their commentaries is this: from the ages of Tang and Yu onward, rulers bore formal titles and posthumous names.
proposals.after: From the time writing was first made, what we can still know of the ancients through the Classics and their commentaries is this: for the ages of Tang and Yu and earlier, rulers bore formal titles and posthumous names.
proposals.reason: Chinese 唐虞以上 means Tang/Yu and earlier ages, not “onward” (later).

proposals.before: Zhang Yan said, "Laozi was deep and silent, and Confucius regarded him as a teacher. Though not ranked among sages, he surely counts as a great worthy. Wenbo's mother mastered the ritual classics; the sage praised her conduct and later ages took her words as a model—yet she appears in the fourth grade. Tian Dan restored great Qi from the isolated city of Jimo; Lu Zhong was broadly learned yet disdained fame and profit; Lord Lin awed King Qin of Qin and yielded to Lian Po—yet they are placed in the fifth grade. Great Ji practiced sorcery and loved sacrificing to ghosts and spirits; the people of Chen were transformed by her and the state was full of improper cults. The eunuch Mengzi, turning from the great elegant style to preserve himself—after castration, wrote in resentment—yet is placed in the third grade. Lao Ai committed incest at court and threw ritual order into chaos, in deeds too foul to bear hearing—yet he is placed in the seventh grade. Discrepancies and errors are many; I have cited a few to expose the faults. Did he gallop alone across thousands of years, looking on at the various masters while his work remained unfinished, then soon meet the Dou family's disaster—and did that make it turn out this way?"

proposals.before: Zhang Yan said: "Laozi was profound and reticent, and Confucius took him as teacher. Though not among the sages, he ought to count as a great worthy. The mother of Wenbo was versed in ritual classics; her conduct won the sage's praise and her words became a model for later ages—yet she is placed in the fourth grade. Tian Dan restored mighty Qi from the lone fortress of Jimo; Lu Zhong was broadly learned yet scorned glory and gain; Lord Lin intimidated King Qin of Qin and yielded ground to Lian Po—yet they are placed in the fifth grade. Great Ji practiced witchcraft and delighted in sacrificing to ghosts and spirits; the people of Chen were transformed by her and the state abounded in licentious worship. The eunuch Mengzi, departing from great elegance to preserve his person—after suffering castration, wrote in resentment and censure—yet is placed in the third grade. Lao Ai committed incest with the sovereign, befouling ritual norms in ways too vile to endure hearing—yet he is placed in the seventh grade. Other discrepancies and errors are numerous; I have raised a few for comparison to expose the mistakes. Did he rush alone through thousands of years, observing the various masters while his work remained incomplete, then soon encounter the Dou family's calamity—which made it come out this way?"

proposals.after: Emperor Ku of the Gaoxin clan
proposals.reason: Idiomatic fuses the personal designation 帝嚳 with clan title 高辛氏 into an unclear compound; literal already separates them.
Parenthetical “(Bo of Yu)” invents an identification not present in 閼伯; idiomatic already has the plain name.
In this person table 陶唐氏 is an individual designation parallel to other named entries; rendering it only as a clan collective obscures that.

decisions.reason: 唐虞以上 means the ages of Tang and Yu and earlier (upward in antiquity), not 'onward'; the proposed English restores that temporal direction.
魯連 is Lu Lian, not Lu Zhong; 秦王 is the King of Qin, not the redundant 'King Qin of Qin'. Both proposed substitutions match the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 魯連之博通……藺子申威秦王

decisions.reason: Same naming errors as in the idiomatic field: 魯連 is Lu Lian and 秦王 is the King of Qin; the proposed literal fixes both without other change.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 魯連之博通……藺子申威秦王

decisions.reason: 帝嚳 and 高辛氏 are distinct designations; fusing them as 'Emperor Ku Gaoxin' is unclear, and 'Emperor Ku of the Gaoxin clan' correctly separates them.
閼伯 supplies only the name E Bo; the parenthetical '(Bo of Yu)' invents an identification absent from the Chinese.
陶唐氏 literally includes the clan marker 氏; 'the Taotang clan' accurately renders that for the literal field, and dropping 'clan' is stylistic rather than correcting an error.

claimRetractions.reason: The fused English personal name 'Emperor Ku Gaoxin' was created only by the unclear idiomatic compound; the accepted repair separates 帝嚳 from 高辛氏.

claimRevisions.reason: The repair preserves 魯連 as the attested shortened name Lu Lian while replacing the erroneous English form Lu Zhong.
The repair corrects the malformed English title while preserving the source-attested title 秦王 as a valid name claim.
